value_text: Mapped planting start dates are seven days before the date with a 50% chance of a freeze.
guidance: Use the local map date; not an observed first-freeze trigger. No Piedmont calendar dates were extracted. Manual location lookup.
source_title: North Carolina Organic Commodities Production Guide: Chapter 4 - Wheat and Small Grains

value_text: A first-freeze-based fly-free date has not worked in North Carolina because freeze timing is unpredictable and may be too late for planting.
guidance: Plant on or after the local dates in Figure 4-1 rather than waiting for the actual first freeze. Manual pest and location check.
source_title: North Carolina Organic Commodities Production Guide: Chapter 4 - Wheat and Small Grains

applies_when: Local regional start date has been read from Figure 1.
guidance: Use Figure 1 to identify the regional start. The guidance allows up to 21 days after that start and advises planting before Thanksgiving. Treat as a manual location check until a mapped date is verified.
source_title: Wheat Planting: NC State University Top Recommendations for High-Yielding Wheat

applies_when: On-time planting with high-quality seed into a conventionally tilled seedbed.
guidance: Target seeding rate, not established plant density. Do not generalize to late planting or broadcasting.

value_text: Soybean is a recommended non-host rotational crop for reducing Fusarium head blight risk.
guidance: NC Extension recommendation; the comparative inoculum study cited in this section was in Minnesota. This is not proof that harvest leaves enough time to plant wheat.
source_title: Planting to Reduce Head Scab Risk
source_locator: Tip 2: Practice good crop rotation with a non-host crop

value_text: Wheat following double-cropped soybean in no-till can have higher Septoria nodorum blotch risk because of residual wheat stubble.
applies_when: No-till wheat follows double-cropped soybean and old wheat residue remains.
guidance: Evaluate more than the immediate previous crop. Manual residue and disease check.

value_text: Soybean planting behind small grain typically occurs from the second week of June through early July.
guidance: Descriptive statewide timing, not a preferred or acceptable exact date range. Keep approximate dates in prose and use actual wheat harvest.

applies_when: Mid-June double-crop planting; 11 NC locations studied in 2019-2021.
guidance: MG4-7 yields were within 5 bu/acre in low- and high-yielding environments. Preserve v1 sb_rc_03 avoiding MG below 4. Select cultivar for desired harvest and disease resistance; not a harvest-date model.

applies_when: Mid-July planting; 11 NC locations studied in 2019-2021.
guidance: MG5-7 had the highest yields at mid-July planting in these trials. Trial-supported ranking, not a guarantee of maturity before frost.

value_text: Yield declines consistently when planting is delayed past the third week of May.
applies_when: General statewide planting-date response also relevant to delayed double-crop planting.
guidance: Not a wheat-specific per-day loss estimate. No numeric daily penalty is supplied by this passage; do not calculate one or treat the full-season optimum as a double-crop planting window.

applies_when: Planting later than mid-June; research plots used 15-inch rows.
guidance: Agronomically yield-maximizing range, not economic optimum or final stand. Applicability is late planting, not a wheat-residue-specific experiment.

value_text: The yield benefit of narrower rows is more pronounced with later planting when emergence-to-pod-set duration is shortened.
guidance: Qualitative late-planting guidance. This passage does not provide a double-crop-specific numerical row-spacing prescription.
source_title: North Carolina Soybean Production Guide: 5. Planting Decisions
